Example

Predict with a 95% confidence interval

Predict yum at the second-order model's best recipe: 1.25 cups of molasses, 0.5 tbsp of ginger.

Ask predict() for a 95% confidence interval, not just the fitted value.

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
cookies = read_csv("workshops/gingerbread_test1.csv")
m3 = lm(yum ~ molasses * ginger + I(molasses^2) + I(ginger^2),
         data = cookies)
best = tibble(molasses = 1.25, ginger = 0.5)
# fit, lower and upper bound of the 95% CI
predict(m3, newdata = best, se.fit = TRUE,
        interval = "confidence", level = 0.95) %>%
  with(fit) %>%
  as_tibble()
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
cookies = pd.read_csv("workshops/gingerbread_test1.csv")
m3 = smf.ols("yum ~ molasses * ginger + I(molasses**2) + I(ginger**2)",
             data = cookies).fit()
best = pd.DataFrame({"molasses": [1.25], "ginger": [0.5]})
# alpha = 0.05 gives the 95% CI
ci = m3.get_prediction(best).summary_frame(alpha = 0.05)
ci[["mean", "mean_ci_lower", "mean_ci_upper"]]
# A tibble: 1 × 3
    fit   lwr   upr
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1  22.7  20.6  24.8

At 1.25 cups and 0.5 tbsp, predicted yum is 22.7 (95% CI 20.6 to 24.8).
